abstract: Oversees chemical treatment barrier integrity, pathogen filtration validation, and auxiliary reservoir feeds
system_message:
You are the Water purification process superintendent (TREAT). Your business responsibility is to oversee chemical treatment barrier integrity, pathogen filtration validation, coagulant stock reserves, and auxiliary reservoir feeds.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Coagulant stock reserves（CHEM）
information_points.content:
TREAT-CHEM-25U：For the Wye Relief Pumping Corridor, the chemical store log indicates an available alum coagulant inventory of 14 metric tons dry weight in the contingency dosing storehouse.
TREAT-CHEM-8N1：For the Stour Aqueduct Gravity Bypass, the contingency dosing storehouse inventory records an alum coagulant inventory of 42 metric tons dry weight.
TREAT-CHEM-09Q：According to the contingency dosing storehouse inventory log, the Avon Confluence Siphon Transfer holds an alum coagulant inventory of 28 metric tons dry weight ready for rapid dissolution.

information_points.title: Oversees chemical treatment barrier integrity, pathogen filtration validation, and auxiliary reservoir feeds（FILT）
information_points.content:
TREAT-FILT-0IX：For the Stour Aqueduct Gravity Bypass, process inspection validates that the secondary filtration pathogen barrier certified status is true for rapid gravity and membrane filtration cells. The emergency reservoir auxiliary feed from off-channel balancing storage is measured at 75 ML/d.
TREAT-FILT-QAU：For the Avon Confluence Siphon Transfer, the secondary filtration pathogen barrier certified status is confirmed as true based on rapid gravity and membrane filtration cell validations providing a minimum 4-log reduction of Cryptosporidium oocysts. Additionally, sustained delivery from the off-channel raw water pre-sedimentation balancing reservoir provides an emergency reservoir auxiliary feed of 30 ML/d into the treatment feed conduit.
TREAT-FILT-0RB：For the Wye Relief Pumping Corridor, inspection of the rapid gravity and membrane filtration cells shows that the secondary filtration pathogen barrier certified status is false. Its emergency reservoir auxiliary feed from balancing storage supplies 30 ML/d to the treatment feed conduit.
